court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court, Mumbai (Case No. not mentioned)
case_name: Shikha Lodha vs Suketu Shah And Anr

parties.respondent_defendant: Suketu Shah, Senior Software Engineer, husband; State of Maharashtra (Respondents)

facts_of_case: Petitioner and respondent got married in Jodhpur, Rajasthan. They stayed in Mumbai with the respondent's parents before the respondent left for U.S.A. The couple separated due to matrimonial issues in 2019. The husband filed a divorce petition in Family Court at Bandra under Section 13 (1) (ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, while the wife filed a divorce petition in U.S.A. which is pending.

legal_principles.principle: The last address of the parties should be taken into consideration for determining jurisdiction.
legal_principles.held: He submitted that even though technically and physically the husband and wife last stayed at U.S.A. but in India they last resided in Mumbai.
cited_cases: MST Jagir Kaur & Another vs. Jaswant Singh, reported in (1964) 2 SCR 73

legal_principles.principle: A wedding reception cannot be considered as a part of marriage ritual.
legal_principles.held: In my view, there can't be any doubt that a wedding reception can't be called as a part of marriage ritual.
cited_cases: Shikha Lodha vs Suketu Shah And Anr on 15 April, 2024

outcome.final_order: The writ petition challenges the judgment and order passed by the Family Court, Mumbai rejecting the application filed by the petitioner (wife) and holding that the Family Court has jurisdiction to entertain and decide the divorce petition filed by the husband.
